review_basis: TYPESET RESULT. papers/D11/paper_draft.pdf (8 pp, 2026-07-30 21:35) rasterised with pdftoppm at 150 and 600 dpi; float placement measured with pdfimages -list; printed glyph sizes measured by connected-component analysis of the 600 dpi raster against a self-calibrated cap/em ratio (0.665, measured by rendering the figure font at a known px size). Standalone PNGs used only to prove byte-level agreement with the current source.
pass_criterion: ALL PASS - zero FAIL and zero MINOR across all four figures and all cross-cutting checks
headline: Every round-4 FAIL is genuinely fixed and independently re-verified; there are ZERO FAILs and ZERO publication-blocking figure defects this round. F3 in particular is closed on both halves: per-trace textfont is normalised, and bundle_figure_typeset_pt now returns the true minimum over every text-bearing field - measurement in the 600 dpi raster confirms the smallest printed string in each figure is 8.66-9.02 pt against 10 pt body, matching the helper's report to within 0.4% (the residual is the helper's 510 pt constant vs the true 507.6-508.2 pt placement). Physics re-derived from formulas.py from scratch: all correct. The highest-priority anchor is CLEAN. What remains is seven MINORs of three kinds - four small label/marker collisions inside figures, and three guard-integrity gaps in the harness (including the fact that the repaired typeset checker has ZERO callers, so the F3 class is fixed but unguarded). Separately, and OUTSIDE figure scope, the rasterised PDF shows a hard two-column collision on page 2 that IS publication-blocking.

round4_remediation_verification.item: F3 - per-trace textfont not covered by the layout contract, and the checker concealed it
round4_remediation_verification.verdict: VERIFIED FIXED, both halves, by two independent methods

No axis title font or tickfont is explicitly set anywhere, so all inherit layout.font; nothing escapes the contract. (b) EMPIRICAL: cap/em ratio self-calibrated at 0.665 by rendering the figure font at 200 px; connected-component measurement of the 600 dpi PDF raster gives legend/label cap heights of 50-53 px = 8.9-9.4 pt em, and x-height clusters of 35 px = 9.4 pt em - agreeing with the analytic prediction to 1-2% and sitting just below the 10 pt body text measured on the same pages. (c) The helper reports 8.925/8.925/9.067/8.693 pt vs true-placed 8.894/8.894/9.023/8.663 pt. It is NOT self-concealing: it now returns the worst string, not the representative one. Spot-checked the shared fix on the D12 three as well: 8.83/8.69/8.69 pt, i.e. the claimed 8.69-9.07 pt across all seven bundle figures is accurate.

physics_reverification.method: Re-derived from src/core/formulas.py from scratch, independent of round 4.
detail: FIG 1 (phononic): diatomic_branches(1,2,1,k) matches 3/2 +- sqrt(5/4 + cos k) to 0.0 max error over 17 k-samples; (0,3) at k=0 and (1,2) at k=pi; phononic_gap_edges() = (1.0,2.0); 20001-point sweep finds ZERO states strictly inside (1,2), acoustic max = 1.0 and optical min = 2.0 so BOTH edges are attained (tight, not loose); rational enclosure (1.0, 1.41) with 1 < 1.41 <= sqrt2 = 1.41421356.

FIG 2 (PT/EP): +-sqrt(1-g^2) real for g<=1, +-sqrt(g^2-1) imaginary beyond; splitting Delta = 2 sqrt(1-g^2) equals exactly 0.2 = 1/5 at g^2 = 99/100, so the enclosure is TIGHT as claimed, and 0 at g = 1. The dotted vline is drawn at g = sqrt(0.99) = 0.99498744, i.e. correctly on the g axis rather than the g^2 axis.

FIG 3 as printed (effective medium): maxwell_garnett(1,4,f) = 1.0 / 2.0 / 4.0 at f = 0 / 1/2 / 1, so the certified point is exact and the constituent bounds are attained at both endpoints (non-strict, as labelled); 2001-point sweep confirms 1 <= eps_eff <= 4 throughout. Voigt >= Reuss on all 2001 points; at f = 2/3, Voigt = 3, Reuss = 2, gap = 1.0 exactly.

FIG 4 as printed (Haldane): haldane_mass_inversion_window(1,pi/2) = 5.196152422706632 = 3 sqrt 3; haldane_dirac_masses gives (m - 3sqrt3, m + 3sqrt3), so blue = 2|m - 3sqrt3 t2 sin phi| zeroes at +3sqrt3 and amber = 2|m + 3sqrt3 t2 sin phi| zeroes at -3sqrt3, matching the plotted zero-crossings and the legend strings; masses are opposite-sign at m = 1 and m = 5 (inside the window) and same-sign at m = 6 (outside).

anchor_checks.anchor: HIGHEST PRIORITY - no Berry curvature, no continuum Chern integral C = (1/2pi) int F, no bulk-boundary result may be depicted OR implied
anchor_checks.evidence: Re-verified from scratch three ways. (1) Programmatic sweep of EVERY string drawn into the four figures - title, axis titles, ticktext, all layout annotations, all trace names, all trace text arrays (14 / 10 / 15 / 14 strings) - against berry curvature|berry connection|bulk-bound|first chern class|continuum chern|edge state|chiral edge|integral sign: ZERO hits in all four. (2) Structural: the Haldane right panel contains only THREE single-point marker traces plus one off-canvas legend proxy (n_finite_x = 1,1,1,0) - there is no continuous C(m) curve anywhere, so nothing interpolates toward a continuum invariant. The y-axis reads 'lattice Chern number C' and the subplot title pins '4x4 torus'. (3) Semantic: the figure's central assertion is that the 4x4 invariant flips at ~3.3177 while the ANALYTIC window edge is 3sqrt3 ~ 5.196 - it actively REFUTES the continuum reading rather than implying it. No boundary, ribbon or edge spectrum is drawn anywhere; the sampled manifold is a closed torus. The bundle's Berry PHASE results (coneBerryPhase_pi) appear only in prose, never in a figure.

cross_cutting.finding: The D11 figures do NOT pass their own registered structural checks. Running the FIGURE_REGISTRY checks against the live figures yields, for d11_fig3_haldane_chern: an ERROR-severity nan_data on trace 2 in both x and y (the legend-proxy trace declared x=[None], y=[None]; np.array([None], dtype=float) is nan), plus an axis_label warning (registry expects yaxis 'Dirac-point gap', actual is 'Dirac gap (units of t)'); and for d11_fig4_effective_medium an axis_label warning (registry expects yaxis 'effective', actual is 'eps<sub>eff</sub> (units of eps_0)'). Nothing is visually wrong - the legend proxy is a deliberate off-canvas entry - but the registry was added in round 2 precisely to be the regression guard, and a guard that reports an ERROR on a correct figure trains the next round to ignore it.
cross_cutting.recommendation: Use x=[], y=[] for the legend proxy (identical legend entry, no NaN), and reconcile the two expected_axes substrings with the actual titles (or relax them to 'Dirac gap' / 'eff').

cross_cutting.finding: bundle_figure_typeset_pt() has ZERO consumers repo-wide - it is called by no structural check, no validate.py check and no test. The F3 repair is therefore correct but UNGUARDED: nothing prevents a future canvas or font edit from silently re-breaching the 8 pt floor, which is exactly the failure mode that survived rounds 1-3. This is the residual half of F3.
cross_cutting.recommendation: Add the assertion to run_structural_checks() - an error-severity CheckIssue when bundle_figure_typeset_pt(fig) < 8.0 for any figure whose layout width is set - so the contract is enforced rather than merely available.

cross_cutting.finding: ANSWER TO THE EXPLICIT QUESTION: yes, I consider the output_dir item still OPEN, but NOT blocking. review_figures.py writes to FIGURES_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT/'figures', so the documented regeneration command does not refresh papers/D11/figures/*.png; the paper's copies and the generated copies can silently diverge. Today they have not - I regenerated all four from current source and got diff_frac = 0.000000 at identical dimensions - which is why this is not blocking. But the risk the round-4 harness fix was meant to remove (documented command reintroduces a stale or wrong-canvas figure) is only half removed: the canvas is now honoured, the destination is not.
cross_cutting.recommendation: Either add output_dir to FigureSpec, or - cheaper and it closes the risk more directly - add a validate.py check asserting that every papers/<bundle>/figures/*.png is byte-identical to a fresh render of its registered function. The sync assertion is what actually protects the paper; output_dir is one way to get there.

summary: Round 5 is a clean round on the figures themselves. All three round-4 FAILs and all five MINORs are verified fixed or verified accepted; there are zero FAILs and zero publication-blocking figure defects. F3 was the systemic one and it is closed on both halves, confirmed independently by enumerating every font field on the live figure objects AND by measuring printed glyph heights in the 600 dpi raster against a self-calibrated cap/em ratio - the smallest printed string per figure is 8.89 / 8.89 / 8.66 / 9.02 pt against 10 pt body, and the helper's report tracks the measurement to within 0.4%. Physics re-derived from formulas.py from scratch is correct in all four. The highest-priority anchor passes on a from-scratch string sweep, on structure (discrete markers, no C(m) curve) and on semantics (the figure refutes the continuum reading). The pass criterion is not met because seven MINORs remain: four are small in-figure label/marker collisions I would accept for publication, and three are harness guard-integrity gaps that do not touch the printed paper but do determine whether these defects can recur. One genuinely blocking defect exists in the PDF and it is NOT a figure: a two-column text collision on page 2.

publication_blocking: R5-8 (two-column collision, p. 2 - prose/LaTeX owner, not figures)
triage.note: If the goal is to ship D11, only R5-8 must be fixed. If the goal is ALL PASS as literally stated, R5-1 through R5-7 are each a small, local change. My own priority order if you fix any subset: R5-8 (blocking), then R5-6 (it is the difference between F3 being fixed and F3 being prevented), then R5-2 (it sits on the central claim), then the rest.

recommendations: R5-8 FIRST and separately: break the long \texttt theorem name at paper_draft.tex:135 so page 2's columns stop colliding. Blocking; owned by prose/LaTeX, not figures.
R5-6: wire bundle_figure_typeset_pt into run_structural_checks() as an error-severity floor at 8.0 pt. Closes the systemic round-4 failure against recurrence.
R5-2: give the Haldane m = 5 and m = 6 labels non-colliding textpositions (e.g. 'bottom left' and 'top right') so neither label's extent sits over the other's marker or across the window boundary.
R5-1: shift the phononic gap annotation clear of the k = -pi upper-edge marker (annotation_xshift, or move it to the band's mid-x).
R5-5: change the Haldane legend proxy to x=[], y=[] and reconcile the two expected_axes substrings with the actual axis titles.
R5-7: add a validate.py check asserting papers/<bundle>/figures/*.png are byte-identical to a fresh render (preferred over, or alongside, FigureSpec.output_dir).
R5-4: give the Reuss trace a distinguishable key (dash pattern or a different palette entry) so the legend key is injective.
R5-3: drop the annotation bgcolor to fully transparent, or move it off the trace, so no data segment is occluded.
root_causes: Corner-collocation: add_hrect / add_vline annotation_position anchors place text in the same corner where the load-bearing edge markers sit (R5-1), and per-point textposition presets do not know about neighbouring points or reference lines (R5-2, R5-3).

Guard availability without guard enforcement: the typeset checker exists and is now correct but is called by nothing (R5-6); the FigureSpec registry exists but its expectations were never reconciled with the figures it guards (R5-5); the harness honours the canvas but not the destination (R5-7).
Long unbreakable \texttt tokens in a two-column class (R5-8) - a prose-side pattern, listed here only because it was found while judging the rasterised PDF.
